**THE FEED** · Thursday 3 September 2026

**GOOGLE CAN BUY ANY AD IT WANTS.  IT JUST SIGNED YOUTUBE'S BIGGEST STAR TO USE ITS PRODUCT ON CAMERA INSTEAD**
Google has signed Jimmy Donaldson — MrBeast — to a multiyear deal to sell Gemini, Google Health and Fitbit.  The company that runs the largest advertising business in history decided the one thing it could not buy any other way was a real person using its product on camera.  The first video drops Friday.

**1.** Google signed MrBeast to a multiyear deal to demonstrate Gemini, Google Health and Fitbit on camera — structure your own creator deals as demonstrations, not endorsements, and sign before the platform bidding war lifts rates.
**2.** Meta shopping-ad spend rose 70 percent while the cost to earn a click fell 18 percent to 13.3 cents — pull your own click-cost trend and make the case for a bigger test budget now, held to a sales target.
**3.** The Chicago Bulls got 1.1 million views in a day on a schedule video built for the group chat — design owned video to be forwarded and rewatched, and measure forwards and rewatches, not just first views.
**4.** MrBeast's novel is on track to bomb at four-figure pre-orders despite 515 million subscribers — price any creator product extension for a cold start unless it asks for the same behaviour that made them fans.
**5.** A carmaker's football tournament hit 4.74 million peak viewers on YouTube, almost all from Vietnam's free feeds — value live-event sponsorships by which markets get an open stream, not by the headline number.
**6.** The RealReal's 9,000-subscriber newsletter has driven 334,000 dollars in tracked sales — start one owned channel with a real voice and measure the revenue that reach alone hides.
**7.** X now forces US creator payouts through its own money app — read the payout and withdrawal terms before routing a creator's fee, because where the money lives is becoming lock-in.
